fixes.explanation: That's not what Isaac asks. He tells Esau to take his quiver and bow and go out into the field to hunt game for him. No night watch here, just a hunting trip. The text says nothing about guarding flocks, so that one's off the menu.

That would be the truth, but it's not what Jacob says. He says, “I am Esau, your firstborn.” (Genesis 27:19) Isaac asked which son he was, and Jacob gives his brother's name. Right brother's name, wrong brother standing there.

Abraham, Isaac's father (Genesis 25:19), isn't in this scene. Isaac says, “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.” (Genesis 27:22) He's talking about the son standing in front of him. His ears are catching on to something.
Isaac doesn't say stranger. He says, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.” (Genesis 27:35) He says it was Esau's brother, plain and simple. No stranger at the door in that line.
There's no servant in Isaac's answer. He says, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.” (Genesis 27:35) He says brother, and he doesn't name him in that line. A servant never comes up.
Esau doesn't ask where Jacob went. He asks, “Do you have only one blessing, my father?” (Genesis 27:38) He's pleading with his father for something of his own. Then he weeps aloud.

That's what Isaac says. “Behold, your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above.” (Genesis 27:39) Compare that to what he said over Jacob, “the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth.” (Genesis 27:28) Same two things, very different words for Esau.

That's not what Isaac says. He tells Esau his dwelling place will be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above. (Genesis 27:39) The plain of the Jordan doesn't come up at all. Isaac's words point away from the richness, not toward it.

Isaac says the opposite. He tells Esau, “…your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land…” (Genesis 27:39) No milk and honey in that line. He's describing a place away from the richness.

Sword. Isaac says, “You shall live by the sword and serve your brother.” (Genesis 27:40) But he isn't done. He adds, “But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck.” (Genesis 27:40) So the words end with a yoke being torn off.

Plow isn't the word. Isaac says, “You shall live by the sword and serve your brother.” (Genesis 27:40) A sword is a harder picture than a plow. And he finishes with a line about a yoke being torn from Esau's neck.

Flock isn't what Isaac says. He tells Esau, “You shall live by the sword and serve your brother.” (Genesis 27:40) It's sword, not flock. Then comes one more line about a yoke being torn from his neck.
